lines.text: A Psalm of Asaph.
The nations, O God, have invaded Your inheritance;
they have defiled Your holy temple
and reduced Jerusalem to rubble.
They have given the corpses of Your servants
as food to the birds of the air,
the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water
all around Jerusalem,
and there is no one to bury the dead.
We have become a reproach to our neighbors,
a scorn and derision to those around us.
How long, O LORD?
Will You be angry forever?
Will Your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out Your wrath on the nations
that do not acknowledge You,
on the kingdoms
that refuse to call on Your name,
for they have devoured Jacob
and devastated his homeland.
Do not hold past sins against us;
let Your compassion come quickly,
for we are brought low.

pictures.scene: David Roberts, The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans Under Titus — the army thrown against the walls while the temple burns above the city, a Psalm of Asaph, the nations O God have invaded Your inheritance
pictures.name: pd_roberts_siege_jerusalem

pictures.scene: Dirck van Delen, Beeldenstorm in een kerk — the men breaking up the holy place and pulling down what stood in it, they have defiled Your holy temple and reduced Jerusalem to rubble
pictures.name: pd_delen_beeldenstorm

pictures.scene: Bruno Liljefors, Sea Eagles — the great birds come down together on what has been left on the shore, they have given the corpses of Your servants as food to the birds of the air
pictures.name: pd_liljefors_sea_eagles

pictures.scene: Wilhelm Kuhnert, Des Löwen Erwachen — the lion risen up out of the grass at first light, the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the earth
pictures.name: pd_kuhnert_loewen_erwachen

pictures.scene: Eugène Delacroix, Hamlet et Horatio au cimetière — the two standing over an opened grave among the bones already turned out of the ground, they have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem
pictures.name: pd_delacroix_hamlet_cimetiere

pictures.scene: Matthias Stom, The Mocking of Christ — the faces crowded in close to jeer at the bound man in the middle, and there is no one to bury the dead, we have become a reproach to our neighbors
pictures.name: pd_stom_mocking_of_christ

pictures.scene: Eduard Bendemann, Die trauernden Juden im Exil — the exiles sitting down together by the water with their heads in their hands, a scorn and derision to those around us, how long O LORD
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_trauernden_juden

pictures.scene: Joachim Patinir, Landscape with the Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah — the fire coming down on the cities of the plain and the smoke going up from them, will You be angry forever, will Your jealousy burn like fire
pictures.name: pd_patinir_sodom_gomorrah

pictures.scene: Hyacinthe Rigaud, Portrait of Louis XIV in Coronation Robes — the king standing in his robes before the throne he has made for himself, pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You
pictures.name: pd_rigaud_louis_xiv

pictures.scene: Jean-Joseph Benjamin-Constant, The Entry of Mahomet II into Constantinople — the conqueror riding into the taken city over everything that was left of it, on the kingdoms that refuse to call on Your name
pictures.name: pd_constant_entree_mahomet

pictures.scene: Andreas Schelfhout, Landschap met de ruïne van kasteel Brederode te Santpoort — the broken castle left standing empty in its own country, for they have devoured Jacob and devastated his homeland
pictures.name: pd_schelfhout_ruine_brederode

pictures.scene: Winslow Homer, The Gulf Stream — the man alone on the broken boat with the sea running under him, do not hold past sins against us, let Your compassion come quickly for we are brought low
pictures.name: pd_homer_gulf_stream
